For a Toronto bridal boutique on a small budget, I’d avoid a big full-service agency and look for someone who can combine short-form content + Meta/Instagram ads, ideally with a low monthly commitment.

Here’s the shortlist I’d investigate:

Provider	Why I’d consider them	Published pricing
Avocado Media	Probably the best budget fit for Instagram/Facebook ads. Their starter package includes 1 campaign, 2 creatives, targeting and optimization.	$400/mo + ad spend 
Avocado Media

HVR Media House	Particularly interesting if Reels are a priority: their Starter package includes 4 short-form videos/month; Growth adds paid-ad management.	$499/mo starter; $999/mo with ads 
HVR Media House

Elyflort	Very small-business oriented. Their entry package includes a Reel and social management, making it inexpensive to test before scaling.	$350/mo 
Elyflort

Rav Link	Their Growth plan combines 12–16 posts, Reels, Meta ads, tracking and optimization—a fairly compelling all-in-one option.	$1,000/mo 
Ravlink

Maduna Marketing	Worth talking to because they specifically position themselves around small businesses and social-driven growth, rather than only enterprise marketing.	Quote-based
Qode Social Media Agency	More agency-style: content creation, paid social, targeting/A-B testing and reporting. They also offer a free social audit.	Quote-based
My top 3 for your situation

1. Avocado Media — if ads are the immediate priority.
At $400/month management, you could keep the actual Meta budget separate and start small. That's attractive if you already have good bridal photos/video and mainly need someone to turn them into campaigns. 
Avocado Media

2. HVR Media House — if you need both Reels and ads.
Their $499 Starter gives you four short-form videos, while their $999 plan adds paid-ad management. For a boutique that needs a steady stream of wedding-content-style creative, that's worth a conversation. 
HVR Media House

3. Elyflort — if $300–$500/month is genuinely your ceiling.
The $350 Mini Social Pack includes an edited Reel from your own material. I'd pair something like this with a very small DIY Meta ad budget rather than paying a large agency retainer. 
Elyflort

One option I'd consider instead of a traditional agency

For a bridal boutique, wedding-specific content creators can actually be a better fit for Reels than a generic social-media agency. For example, The Sarah Jane Co. works with Toronto/GTA wedding vendors and offers a 2-hour BTS content package for $400, including raw vertical footage and a highlight Reel; 4 hours is $600 with two highlight Reels. 
The Sarah Jane

That could give you a bank of authentic dress try-ons, appointment moments, veil reveals, new-arrival videos and behind-the-scenes footage that an ads specialist can then turn into Meta creatives.

If I were allocating a small budget: I'd probably do $400–600 for content + $300–500/month in actual Meta ad spend, rather than spending $1,500–3,000+ on an agency retainer. The creative is especially important for bridal—beautiful, native-looking Reels can do double duty as organic content and ad creative.

If you tell me your approximate monthly budget (e.g. $500, $1,000, or $2,000 all-in), I can narrow this to 3 Toronto providers and compare exactly what you'd get from each.
